findings.description: The EBS volume does not set `encrypted = true` or a KMS key. Its encryption therefore depends on the account-level EBS encryption-by-default setting, which is not established in this excerpt; data stored on this attached portal disk may be unencrypted at rest.

This subnet assigns public IPv4 addresses to instances at launch and is associated with a route table containing a default route through an Internet Gateway. Instances launched here can become Internet-reachable if their security groups permit traffic.

The instance user-data embeds an AWS access key ID and secret access key. User data is stored in instance metadata and Terraform state/context, exposing long-lived credentials to users or processes that can read them; the credentials may also be recoverable from the deployed host.
TCP/22 is permitted from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing administrative SSH access to any Internet host when the instance is publicly reachable through the declared Internet gateway and route infrastructure.

TCP/80 is permitted from 0.0.0.0/0. The instance installs and starts Apache, so this exposes the web service to all Internet sources when the associated subnet is routed through the declared Internet gateway.

The security group permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0. This removes egress network controls for the Internet-facing instance, enabling unrestricted outbound connections if it is compromised.

The S3 bucket used as the VPC flow-log destination has no server-side encryption configuration. Flow-log records stored in the archive therefore are not explicitly protected with a customer-managed or bucket-enforced encryption setting.

The snapshot does not set encrypted storage or an encryption key. Although it may inherit encryption from the source volume in some cases, this excerpt does not establish that aws_ebs_volume.portal_server_disk is encrypted, so the backup's encryption at rest cannot be assured.
